projects.title: 6-DOF Robotic Arm
projects.tagline: Custom-engineered 6-DOF robotic arm with 27:1 cycloidal gearboxes, 450 mm reach, and 0.6 kg payload.
projects.summary: A fully functional, 6-DOF desktop robotic arm engineered from first-principles mechanics, featuring custom-designed 27:1 cycloidal reducers integrated directly into the structural links. Built with an inverted cobot topology, the arm achieves a 450 mm radial reach and a 0.60 kg payload capacity (0.90 kg total tip load). The entire mechanical structure is optimized for FDM 3D printing in PETG, incorporating complete bearing load isolation, dynamic counter-balancing, and thermal creep prevention.
features: 6-DOF anthropomorphic cobot topology (UR-style offset pitch-pitch-pitch layout)
Custom single-stage 27:1 cycloidal gearboxes with dual 180° dynamically balanced discs
Ultra-flat cycloidal torque transmission with only 0.52° pressure angle variation
Dual 6808 thin-section ball bearings per joint for full cantilever moment isolation
Inverted rotating-housing architecture where link bodies serve as stator gear rings
Modular link design allowing the identical C-joint to serve as both Upper Arm and Forearm
24V electrical bus with current-derated NEMA 17 steppers to eliminate PETG thermal creep
Integrated synchronized parallel gripper (Scotch-yoke servo drive, 40 mm stroke, >12 N pinch force)
Designed for direct URDF generation and ROS 2 / MoveIt 2 simulation integration
projects.architecture: The arm utilizes a modular "bridge" architecture where each link houses the cycloidal reducer of the current joint on one end and the motor of the next joint on the other. Motors directly drive cycloidal cams without belts, pulleys, or separate couplers. Joint 1 employs an inverted drive with the pin cage anchored to the base, forcing the shoulder housing to rotate. High-torque NEMA 17 motors power the heavy base axes while lightweight pancake steppers minimize wrist inertia, all supported by standard ISO deep-groove and thin-section bearings, hardened steel dowel pins, and brass heat-set inserts.
projects.results:
- Torque Performance: Delivered 10.8 Nm peak torque at Joint 2, exceeding the 10.5 Nm worst-case dynamic holding requirement with positive safety margins.
- Structural Rigidity: Achieved >6.0 mm nominal wall thickness around all motor corners and >8.5 mm around bearing seats, preventing FDM layer flex under full load.
- CAD Maturity: 100% completed SolidWorks parametric assembly with zero internal clashes, fully validated for URDF kinematic export and physical fabrication.

projects.title: WD Drone: TEKNOFEST 2026
projects.tagline: Autonomous rotary-wing UAV for the TEKNOFEST rotary-wing category
projects.role: Founding team member, simulation and systems integration (team of six)
projects.summary: A rotary-wing UAV built by a six-member team across mechanical, avionics, software and computer vision. I built the Gazebo/ArduPilot SITL environment, integrated the companion computer and flight controller, developed the target detection, and contributed to mechanical design and structural FEA.
features: Custom Gazebo/ArduPilot SITL for waypoint survey, target approach, payload delivery and RTL
Raspberry Pi 5, Camera Module 3 and Cube Orange integrated through MAVLink/pymavlink
OpenCV colour and geometric target detection at about 30 FPS
Velocity corrections generated from target-centre offsets
Autonomous waypoint flight with AUTO/GUIDED/RTL transitions
projects.architecture: The Pi 5 captures frames from the Camera Module 3 and runs OpenCV detection. Target-centre offsets become velocity corrections that pymavlink sends to the Cube Orange flight controller. Every mission stage was rehearsed in SITL before physical flight.
projects.results: Five flight-test sessions at about 3–10 m altitude covered autonomous flight, target detection and payload release. Structural FEA on the 5 mm carbon-fibre arm plates and 3 mm central-body plates under an 8 kg static load gave a peak von Mises stress of 24.9 MPa. A 1,500 g motor-thrust test and an 8 kg static-load test verified propulsion and structure on the real airframe.

projects.title: 3-DOF SCARA Robotic Arm
projects.tagline: Designed, printed, programmed and tested as a graduation project
projects.summary: A 3-DOF SCARA arm with 492.5 mm reach, a vertical Z-axis and a servo gripper. I handled mechanical design, manufacturing, electronics, firmware and system integration on my own.
features: Two-stage GT2 belt/gear transmission with NEMA 17 steppers and DRV8825 drivers
DFM applied to print orientation, supports, tolerances and bearing fits
ESP32 firmware in C++: forward and inverse kinematics, homing, motion limits, gripper control
Engineering drawings, BOM and manufacturing-ready CAD
Integrated with a mobile robot and conveyor over a three-node MQTT network
projects.architecture: Joint torque calculations guided motor selection. Links were topology-optimized, printed in PLA+ and post-processed with sanding, drilling, reaming, heat-set inserts and tapping. An ESP32 runs the kinematics and stepper control and talks to the mobile robot and conveyor over MQTT.
projects.results: Topology optimization reduced the mass of the arm link by 16.5% (201 g to 168 g) while keeping the mounting and load-bearing regions. The revised links were manufactured and tested, the arm held a 100 g payload at full extension, and the three-node system demonstrated autonomous box transfer and shelving.
